translation_notes: MAIN FINDING (negative): `obsgraph` is a module-level graph and the region is a function, so ldpy's `G += g{ ... }` idiom turns `obsgraph` into a local and raises UnboundLocalError. The translation therefore has to add `global obsgraph` -- one statement the original does not have. Semantics are unchanged (rdflib's Graph.__iadd__ returns self, so the rebinding is a no-op), but 'module-level graph + helper functions that add to it' is a very common rdflib layout, and the augmented-assignment idiom does not reach it for free. `obsgraph.__iadd__(g{ ... })` is the alternative that needs no declaration, at the price of a dunder call.

prefixes: sosa: taken from PySOSA/config.py (cfg.sosa), rdfs: from rdflib. cfg.sosa.Actuator/observes/implements -> sosa:Actuator/observes/implements, RDF.type -> a, RDFS.comment/label -> rdfs:comment/label; RDF and RDFS are dropped from the rdflib import since they become dead.
the three consecutive obsgraph.add() calls with the same subject merge into one island with `;`; the two adds inside the for loops stay one-line islands, since their control flow is preserved.

BNode() and Literal(args[i]) are kept as Python: they are stored on the instance (self.actuator_id, self.label, ...) and only then used as terms, so the notation cannot absorb them. Inside the island they are interpolated as {self.actuator_id}, {self.comment}, {self.label}, {act.label}. This is the common shape in constructor code and it caps how much of a class's RDF work the notation can take over.

the upstream bug in the last loop (`self.sensor_id`, which an Actuator never sets) is preserved verbatim. It is unreachable: `self.procedure = Literal(args[3])` makes the loop iterate over the characters of a string, which are never Procedure instances. The demo harness does not trigger it either.

demo harness added identically to both representations: __init__ returns nothing and writes into the module-level obsgraph, so the harness calls it on a bare instance with one ActuatableProperty and one non-ActuatableProperty (to exercise the isinstance guard); the resulting 4-triple obsgraph is what the driver compares.
the region's imports are left exactly as upstream; the driver puts the corpus checkout of commit 1993668bd7 on sys.path (with sys.dont_write_bytecode) so PySOSA resolves to the real, pinned package.

driver deviation, identical for both sides: config.get_graph() upstream returns one module-level Graph. The harness executes both modules in the same process, so they would share and accumulate into it and the comparison would be vacuous; the driver replaces get_graph by a factory returning a fresh Graph.
